svg.text: Every layer of a ResNet moves the signal less than its plain equivalent does
Standard deviation of layer responses on CIFAR-10, sorted by magnitude
response = output of each 3x3 layer, after BN and before the ReLU or the addition
rank: layers sorted by std, largest first — std on the y axis

g.data-tip: The two plain networks sit highest: every layer changes the signal by a lot. Residual nets sit visibly below them at the same depth.
The residual networks sit lower, and the deeper the ResNet the lower it sits. The paper: when there are more layers, an individual layer of ResNets tends to modify the signal less.

svg.text: Redrawn from Figure 7, lower panel; curve shapes schematic.
VERDICT: LITTLE WEIGHT ON ITS OWN
Figure 7 shows the pattern the hypothesis predicts, but nothing
rules out other causes. A consistency check, not a test.

a.data-tiphead: Hypothesis, support, and the gap between them
a.data-tip: Section 3.1 states the intuition as a hypothesis and Section 4.2 offers the response magnitudes as support. The paper never claims to have isolated the mechanism.
a.text: Argument by construction, evidence by correlation
THE HYPOTHESIS, SEC 3.1
The authors hypothesize that it is easier to optimize the
residual mapping than the original, unreferenced mapping.
THE SUPPORT, SEC 4.2
In a ResNet, the second layer's response is F(x) itself.
ResNets have generally smaller responses than their plain
counterparts, and deeper ResNets smaller still. The chain:
small std of F(x) → F changes x little → near identity.
WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH
There is no ablation in the paper that turns the mechanism off.
BN's learned scale sets each std directly, so a small
response is the solver picking a small scale: consistent
with the hypothesis, not proof of it. The paper's own
wording is hedged: hypothesize, then might.

a.data-tip: Veit, Wilber and Belongie argued a ResNet behaves like an ensemble of relatively shallow networks; Balduzzi et al. described shattered gradients in plain nets; Li et al. visualised skip connections smoothing the loss landscape. All of them postdate this paper.
a.text: The result held; the explanation did not settle
Later accounts attribute the gain to ensembles of shallow
paths, to gradients staying correlated rather than shattering,
and to a smoother loss landscape. Slide 23 lists them with
links; none of them existed when this paper was written.
